senses.gloss:
यक् यक्, (in grammar) a term for the
syllable य, which is the sign of the Passive.

यकन् यकन्, a defective word optionally
substituted for यकृत् in certain cases. See below.

यकृत् यकृत्, त्, n. (all the cases except the
Nom. Voc. sing. du. pl., Acc. sing. du. are optionally
formed from a base यकन्, hence Acc. pl. यकृन्ति
or यकानि, Inst. sing. du. pl. यकृता or यक्ना, य-
कृद्भ्याम् or यकभ्याम्, यकृद्भिस् or यक-
भिस्, see Pāṇ. VI. 1, 63, Vopa-deva III. 39, III. 165,
Gram. 144), the liver; [cf. Gr. ἧπαρ; Lat. jecur;
(perhaps) Angl. Sax. lifer; Lett. ak-ni-s; Bohem.
jatra, ‘the liver.’]
—यकृत्-कोश, अस्, अम्, m. n.
the cyst or membrane enveloping the liver.
—य-
कृद्-आत्मिका, f. a kind of cockroach.
—यकृद्-
उदर or यकृद्-दाल्य or यकृद्-दाल्य्-उदर,
अम्, n. an enlargement of the liver.
—यकृद्-वर्ण,
अस्, आ, अम्, liver-coloured, of the colour of liver.
—यकृद्-वैरिन्, ई, m. Andersonia Rohitaka.
—यकृन्-मेदस्, अस्, n. liver and fat.
—यकृल्-
लोम, आस्, or यकृल्-लोमन्, आनस्, m. pl., N. of
a people.

यक्ष् यक्ष् (connected with rt. 1. यज्),
cl. 1. P. यक्षति, (according to some
originally) to move, stir (as a living being); to
honour; cl. 10. A. यक्षयते, अययक्षत, &c.,
to worship, honour; (according to Sāy. प्र-यक्-
षन्त in Ṛg-veda 1. 132, 5 = प्रकर्षेण
यजन्ते, they diligently worship.)

यक्ष, अम्, n. (the neut. form is found only in
Ved.), a living supernatural being (or a being deserv-
ing of worship, cf. rt. 1. यज्), an unsubstantial or
spiritual apparition, a ghost, spirit; (according to
Sāy.) worship, adoration (= पूजा); sacrifice (=
यज्ञ); anything honoured or revered; (अस्), m.,
N. of certain mythical beings or demigods who,
like the Guhyakas, are attendants on Kuvera, the
god of wealth, and employed in the care of his
garden and treasures, (they are variously described
as sons of Pulastya, of Pulaha, of Krodhā, of Kaś-
yapa; or in Hari-vaṃśa 11794. as sprung from the
feet of Brahmā; according to the Vāyu-Purāṇa they
were descended from Khasā or Khaśā, who had two
sons, Yakṣa and Rakṣas, severally the progenitors
of the Yakṣas and Rākṣasas; the Viṣṇu-Purāṇa
1. 5. narrates that they were produced by Brahmā as
beings emaciate with hunger, of hideous aspect, and
with long beards, and that crying out ‘let us eat,’
they were denominated Yakṣas, [fr. जक्ष्, to eat];
in the Brahma-Purāṇa thirteen Yakṣas are appointed
[]
by Viṣṇu as guardians of a particular city; though
generally regarded as beings of a benevolent and
inoffensive disposition, like the Yakṣa described in
Kālidāsa's Megha-dūta, they are nevertheless occa-
sionally classed with Piśācas and other malignant
spirits; the Buddhists give them a prominent posi-
tion, describing them in some of their legends as
cruel demons who feast on human flesh and have
the power of raising storms; in others, as harmless
beings who delight in songs, dances, &c.); a sub-
division of a Vyantara (with Jainas); N. of Kuvera;
of a Muni; of the palace of Indra; (ई), f. a female
Yakṣa; N. of Kuvera's wife; (अस्, आ, अम्), a Vedic
word said to be formed fr. the Aor. of rt. 1. यज्,
and used at the end of a comp.
—यक्ष-कर्-
दम, अस्, m. an ointment or perfumed paste con-
sisting of camphor, agallochum, musk, and kakkola,
or, according to some, saffron, in equal proportions;
(according to others the ointment also contains
sandal-wood.)
—यक्ष-कूप, अस्, m. ‘Yakṣa-
tank,’ N. of a place.
—यक्ष-ग्रह, अस्, m. ‘the
being possessed by Yakṣas,’ N. of a particular kind
of insanity.
—यक्षग्रह-परिपीडित, अस्, आ, अम्,
afflicted with the preceding insanity.
—यक्ष-तरु,
उस्, m. ‘Yakṣa-tree, ’ the Indian fig-tree.
—यक्ष-
ता, f. or यक्ष-त्व, अम्, n. the state or condition
of a Yakṣa, the being a Yakṣa.
—यक्ष-दर,
N. of a district.
—यक्ष-दासी, f., N. of a wife of
Śūdraka.
—यक्ष-दृश्, क्, क्, क्, Ved. having the
look or appearance of a Yakṣa, having a living or
visible appearance, bodily, corporeal, (but according
to Sāy. = उत्सवस्य द्रष्टा, a gazer or spectator
at a festival.)
—यक्ष-धूप, अस्, m. the resin of
Shorea Robusta; resin in general; incense.
—यक्-
ष-नायक, अस्, m., N. of the servant of the fourth
Arhat of the present Ava-sarpiṇī.
—यक्ष-पति,
इस्, m. a king of the Yakṣas; N. of Kuvera.
—यक्ष-पाल, अस्, m., N. of a king.
—यक्ष-
बलि, इस्, m. an oblation to the Yakṣas.
—यक्ष-
भृत्, त्, त्, त्, Ved. ‘Yakṣa-bearing,’ nourishing or
supporting the Yakṣas; receiving worship, receiving
that which is honoured; (Sāy. = पूजितं हविर्-
आदिकं दधानः.)
—यक्ष-मल्ल, अस्, m. (with
Buddhists) N. of one of the five Lokeśvaras.
—यक्-
ष-रस, अस्, m. a kind of intoxicating drink.
—यक्ष-राज्, ट्, m. ‘king of the Yakṣas,’ N. of
Kuvera; of Maṇi-bhadra; a palæstrum or place pre-
pared for wrestling and boxing.
—यक्ष-राज, अस्,
m. ‘Yakṣa-king,’ N. of Kuvera.
—यक्षराट्-पुरी,
f., N. of Alakā, the capital of Kuvera (supposed to
be situated on mount Kailāsa).
—यक्ष-रात्रि, इस्,
f. ‘the night of the Yakṣas,’ N. of a Hindū festival
(= दीपाली, q. v.).
—यक्ष-वर्मन्, आ, m., N. of
a commentator on Śākaṭāyana.
—यक्ष-वित्त, अस्,
आ, अम्, one whose property is like that of the Yakṣas,
one who has merely the guardianship of property
and does not make use of it himself.
—यक्ष-
सेन, अस्, m., N. of a king.
—यक्ष-स्थल, अस्,
m. (?), N. of a place.
—यक्षाङ्गना (˚ष-अङ्˚),
f. a Yakṣa woman.
—यक्षाङ्गी (˚ष-अङ्˚), f.,
N. of a river.
—यक्षाधिप (˚ष-अध्˚), अस् or
यक्षाधिपति (˚ष-अध्˚), इस्, m. ‘lord of the
Yakṣas,’ N. of Vaiśravaṇa or Kuvera.
—यक्षा-
मलक (˚ष-आम्˚), अम्, n. the fruit of a species
of date called Piṇḍa-kharjūra.
—यक्षावास (˚ष-
आव्˚), अस्, m. ‘the abode or residence of the Yakṣas,’
the Indian fig-tree.
—यक्षी-त्व, अम्, n. the state
or condition of a female Yakṣa, the being a Yakṣī.
—यक्षेन्द्र (˚ष-इन्˚), अस्, m. a king of the
Yakṣas; N. of Kuvera.
—यक्षेश् (˚ष-ईश्), ट्,
m., N. of the servants of the eleventh and eighteenth
Arhat of the present Ava-sarpiṇī.
—यक्षेश (˚ष-
ईश) or यक्षेश्वर (˚ष-ईश्˚), अस्, m. a king of
the Yakṣas; N. of Kuvera.
—यक्षोडुम्बरक
(˚ष-उड्˚), अम्, n. the fruit of the Ficus Religiosa.

याक्ष याक्ष, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. यक्ष), be-
longing or peculiar to the Yakṣas.

यक्षक, अस्, m. = यक्ष, N. of certain mythi-
cal beings attending on Kuvera.
यक्षण, अम्, n. probably for जक्षण, q. v.
यक्षन्, probably for यक्ष्मन्, q. v.

यक्षिन्, ई, इणी, इ, having life, living, really exist-
ing (said of Varuṇa); adorable, (Sāy. = यजनीय);
[]
(इणी), f. = यक्षी, a female Yakṣa; N. of Kuvera's
wife; a sort of female fiend attached to the service
of Durgā and frequently, like a sylph or fairy, main-
taining intercourse with mortals.
—यक्षिणी-त्व,
अम्, n. the state or condition of a female Yakṣa,
the being a Yakṣī.

यक्षु, उस्, m., अवस्, m. pl., N. of a family or
race.

यक्ष्म, अस्, m. sickness, disease in general or
N. of a large class of diseases (probably of a con-
sumptive nature); pulmonary disease, consumption.
—यक्ष्म-नाशन, अस्, ई, अम्, Ved. destroying
or removing sickness; (अस्), m. the reputed author
of the hymn Ṛg-veda X. 161, (having the patro-
nymic Prājāpatya.)

यक्ष्मन्, आ, m. pulmonary consumption, con-
sumption, decline (= शोष, क्षय).
—यक्ष्म-
गृहीत, अस्, आ, अम्, seized with consumption, afflicted
with or suffering from consumption.
—यक्ष्म-
ग्रस्त, अस्, आ, अम्, attacked by consumption.
—य-
क्ष्म-ग्रह, अस्, m. a consumptive seizure, attack
of consumption.
—यक्ष्म-घ्नी, f. ‘destroying
consumption,’ grapes, raisins.
यक्ष्मोधा, f. a kind of sickness.

यक्ष्य यक्ष्य, यक्ष्यमाण. See under
rt. 1. यज्.

यक्ष्य, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. to be sacrificed or wor-
shipped, &c., (according to Sāy. on Ṛg-veda VIII.
60, 3 = यष्टव्य.)

यक्ष्यमाण, अस्, आ, अम्, about to perform a
sacrifice, wishing to make a sacrifice.

याकृत्क याकृत्क (fr. यकृत्), see Pāṇ. VII.
3, 51.
